To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The Cosine Similarity and the Multiscale Cosin Similarity Entropies (CSE and MCSE) are superior to the Sample Entropy (SSE) for short time series.

the CSE and MCSE provide a more accurate and reliable quantification of structural entropy of dynamical systems and that the MCSE offers an enhanced quantification over a broad range, including the short time series case.
the CSE and MCSE are amplitude independent, robust to noise, and are able to estimate degrees of structural complexity over small to large scales.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and validation of new entropy estimations based on the angular distance, for the quantification and characterization of the structural complexity in dynamical systems.
the analysis of the complexity of non-stationary signals and the characterization of its dynamics.
the development of new tools for the analysis of complex systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the CSE and MCSE are more robust than the SE, and are able to quantify degrees in structural complexity in the presence of noise, even for short data segments.

the CSE is an entropy measure based on correlation and not on uncertainty, and therefore is a more appropriate estimator for the quantification and understanding of the structural complexity in dynamical systems.

, in the context of structural complexity, the CSE and MCSE are more robust and more reliable estimators of the underlying structure than the SE, in the sense of being less sensitive to noise, spikes and erratic peaks and being able to estimate entropy values over small to large scales.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we propose the CSE and MCSE for quantification of structural (self) correlation complexity in dynamical systems and that we demonstrate that the CSE and its multiscale generalization are superior to SE in terms of precision, reliability and computational efficiency.

the CSE and MCSE are more reliable and efficient than the SE for quantification of complexity of nonstationarity and long term correlated time series, and thus can be used for a wide variety of biomedical signal processing applications.

we propose a new class of entropy measures that can be applied to short time-series, and can be used to quantify the complexity of a dynamical system in terms of the number of its active degrees of freedom.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the CSE and MCSE are able to provide a reliable quantification of structural properties of dynamical systems, and therefore can serve as a powerful tool for the analysis and interpretation of real world data.
the CSE and MCSE are able to quantify the structural complexity of signals with long term correlation and short time series, which is a major improvement over the SE.

self correlation based measures, such as the proposed CSE and the enhanced MCSE, offer a more reliable and physically sound alternative to the SE, especially for the quantification and analysis of the intrinsic complexity of short time series.
